label: j re-fed as copy input at the 2nd/3rd copy step (j was orig token 0 or 1)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the input token is j and the step is recall_idx 1 or 2, i.e. the model is re-reading a j that was the first or second original token. Strongest (~0.9-1.0 of max, ~82% of mass) when j was the first original token (step L+1, right after <DEL>). Weaker (~0.05-0.35 of max) when j was the second original token (step L+2); there magnitude grows with L. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, on any token other than j, or on j later in the copy (except 17 negligible activations at recall_idx 3). Most false positives are j at recall_idx 2 in short sequences (L=3-4).

issues: Most of the claims hold up. All activation mass is in the copy phase, in_tok is always j, and nothing fires on non-j tokens or in the original/delimiter phases. Recall_idx 1 holds 0.819 of the mass and recall_idx 2 holds 0.181. Recall_idx 3 has only 17 negligible activations.

There is one systematic class of false positives: j at recall_idx 2 when L=3. That subset has precision 0.019 on dev (413 predicted steps, 8 active), so the feature essentially never fires there. The explanation only says false positives are 'mostly short sequences (L=3-4)'. It does not state that L=3 is a hard exclusion, and the predicate does not encode it.
At L=4, recall_idx 2 has precision 0.82. That is a softer, partial drop-off. The remaining false positives (e.g. 'q j y h <DEL> q j') show no obvious token pattern.
The predicate is precise for every other case: recall_idx 1 has precision 1.0 at every L, and recall_idx 2 has precision 1.0 for L=5-9.
The label overclaims slightly. 'j re-fed at the 3rd copy step (j was orig token 1)' is false when L=3.
The claim that the recall_idx-2 activation 'rises with L' was not checked systematically. The original agent said so themselves, so it should not be stated as fact.
Missed activations on test are scattered noise: 19 steps, 0.0% of the mass, all tiny j activations at recall_idx 3.
skeptic.revised_label: j re-fed as a copy input when j was original token 0 (strong) or original token 1 (weaker; absent when L=3, partial when L=4)

final_label: j re-fed as a copy input when j was original token 0 (strong) or original token 1 (weaker; absent when L=3, partial when L=4)
